chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Uthman ibn Jabala, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three characteristics: whoever possesses them, or even one of them, will be in the shade of the Throne of Allah on the Day when there is no shade except His. [They are:] A man who gives people from himself what they ask of him; and a man who does not move forward a step nor backward a step until he knows that this is for the pleasure of Allah; and a man who does not find fault with his Muslim brother for a defect until he removes that defect from his own self, for indeed he does not remove one defect from it except that another defect becomes apparent to him, and sufficient for a man is occupation with his own self [rather than finding fault] with people.'

key_terms.ظِلِّ عَرْشِ اللَّهِ: Shade of the Throne of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that ensure a person is in the Shade of Allah's Throne on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights three spiritual virtues—selfless generosity, pure intentionality (ikhlas), and constructive criticism through self-correction—that secure a believer's place under Allah's Throne. The final trait emphasizes the principle of 'self-occupation' (shughl bi-nafs), suggesting that focusing on one's own flaws is a more effective path to moral integrity than scrutinizing others, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings.
